title: A FAITHFUL SERVANT LAID TO REST

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: At the Lord's command Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor, where he died on the first day of the fifth month of the fortieth year after the Israelites came out of Egypt. Aaron was a hundred and twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor. The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming. - Num 33:38-40 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In the middle of the travel record, we pause for a death. Aaron, Israel's first high priest, climbed Mount Hor at the Lord's command and died there at the age of a hundred and twenty-three. It is striking that this is one of only two dates given a precise timestamp in the whole chapter. Aaron's life mattered; his death was marked and remembered. A faithful servant of God had finished his course.

Aaron was not a perfect man — he had failed at times, including the golden calf. Yet God used him greatly as the priest who represented the people before God and offered sacrifices on their behalf. Now his ministry passed to his son, and the work of God continued. No single servant is indispensable; God's purposes carry on from one generation to the next.

Aaron's priesthood, precious as it was, could never fully take away sin. Year after year the sacrifices had to be repeated, because the blood of animals could not truly cleanse the conscience. Aaron himself died, as every earthly priest must. But the writer of Hebrews points us to a better High Priest — Jesus, who lives forever and whose single sacrifice deals with sin completely (Heb 7:23-25).

Where Aaron's ministry ended in death on a mountain, Christ's ministry continues eternally at God's right hand. He always lives to intercede for us. We have a High Priest who never dies, never fails, and never stops praying for His people. What comfort to be held by such a Priest.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What does Aaron's life teach you about being a faithful, though imperfect, servant?
2. How does Jesus, the High Priest who lives forever, give you assurance?
3. Are you resting in Christ's finished and ongoing work rather than in any human leader?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for faithful servants who finish their course, and above all for Jesus, my eternal High Priest who always lives to intercede for me. Help me to rest in His perfect and unending work. Amen.
